span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cooling VLPFC silences a small anterolateral zone where auditory and multisensory cells are concentrated while visual cells, being spread across dorsal and ventral prefrontal cortex, keep working — producing an auditory/audiovisual deficit with visual memory spared.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Holding an acoustic stimulus already consumes VLPFC storage, so adding a face to remember exhausts the remaining capacity there and the extra item fails when VLPFC is inactivated.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Match enhancement appears earlier in prefrontal cortex than in temporal pole or primary auditory cortex, implying prefrontal top-down feedback drives the mnemonic modulation of the auditory circuit.

'ALTHOUGH NHP'S AUDITORY MEMORY ABILITIES MAY BE LESS THAN THEIR CAPACITIES FOR REMEMBERING VISUAL INFORMATION they have demonstrated the ability to DISCRIMINATE AND REMEMBER AUDITORY SOUNDS OVER SEVERAL SECONDS, WHICH IS, BY DEFINITION, AUDITORY WORKING ME[MORY].' span.label: RETRACTED (THE `from` ENDPOINT IS OVER-SPECIFIED AND UNATTESTED) · decay —contrasted-with→ proactive interference
span.note: RETRACTED: THE `from` ENDPOINT IS OVER-SPECIFIED AND UNATTESTED. The edge is `decay --contrasted-with--> proactive interference`. The span: 'It has been suggested that Quotation withheld (Lewandowsky et al., 2008), but a recent study examining memory for timbre found that DECAY DOES PLAY A ROLE.' The contrast is real and well drawn - interference against decay, with a citation on each side - AND THE SPAN SAYS `INTERFERENCE`, NOT `PROACTIVE INTERFERENCE`. Proactive interference is a specific kind, distinguished in this literature from retroactive; the qualifier was supplied. TRUE OF THE FIELD, NOT IN THE SPAN, and the endpoint test caught it where reading past it would not have. Q-433. — strength of the relation: 0.95

span.label: humans show steeper forgetting curves for auditory than visual material, as monkeys do
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE SUBJECT OF THIS RESULT IS AN INDEFINITE STUDY, NOT THIS PAPER. `Previous studies reported`, `studies in guinea pig showed`, `recent studies have reported` - somebody else's work under a common noun rather than a name, with a citation in the sentence and no first-person marker. The quote is verbatim and the claim is true; only the attribution is wrong. FOUND BY MEASURING MY OWN CUE'S RECALL: the first sweep required a NAMED author as the subject (`Sperling (1960) demonstrated`) and found 17. Reading eleven citation-bearing findings on `Plakke2016` by hand showed four the cue could not see - `A study examining recognition found`, `studies of typical human subjects have demonstrated`, `A follow up study found` - so the named cue's 17 was a floor and not a count. A CUE'S FALSE POSITIVES TELL YOU NOTHING ABOUT ITS FALSE NEGATIVES, and the only way to find these was to read a record's whole layer. Q-1118.

span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: match suppression at an early latency of 31-60 ms ( Ng et al., 2014 ). - 2026-08-26 terminal-a. THE RESULT IS THE CITED WORK'S AND THE CITATION TRAILS THE SENTENCE. A plain noun phrase is the subject of the result verb and the attribution is a bracket at the end - `Neurons within the dorsal temporal pole demonstrated match suppression ... ( Ng et al., 2014 )`. Neither of my two cues could see this shape, so THESE WERE READ RATHER THAN SWEPT: 36 candidates of the shape, 20 read, 11 marked, 9 refused. THE REFUSALS ARE WHY IT IS NOT A CUE: `Aru2012 findings[16]` is the paper's OWN result with a citation supporting the localisation, `Natan2015 findings[3]` ends `consistent with previous findings ( Szymanski et al., 2009 )` where the main clause is the paper's, and `Drieu2019` x3 are `One cannot entirely rule out...` - a limitation, not an attribution. About 55% precise, which is a list to read and not a sweep to run. Q-1119.
